items.obligation: resolveConflict must prune the settled id from ProjectState.blocking_conflict_ids the way applyChange:547-557 does, and must not let any APPLIED change settle any conflict, and must not let a RESOLVED conflict be settled again
items.product_change: internal/domain/changes.go: resolveConflict gained an OPEN-status guard, a relation check against a new disputedScope/settlesDispute pair, and the blocking_conflict_ids prune. disputedScope is the entity ids the conflict names as subjects or blocked, plus the (entity, id, field) triples edited by any ChangeProposal among its subjects; settlesDispute also accepts a proposal that declared the conflict in its own conflict_ids, which is the relation applyChange already uses.
items.why_the_impossible_guard_stayed_removed: ResolveConflictRequest carries only resolution_proposal_id and reason (frozen schema, spec/v2.0/contracts/domain.schema.json), so the original guard that demanded the conflict already name the proposal could never be satisfied. Round 1 was right about that; what was wrong was replacing it with no relation check at all.
items.fixture_note: the unrelated settler is a revision of a requirement nothing depends on, not the requirement revision used later in the phase. Revising THAT requirement makes the decisions pinning it non-effective, and the second draft proposes exactly such a decision - measured as 412 STALE_INPUT 'input version changed'. CHG-UNRELATED-CHANGE-STALES-NOTHING-HERE keeps the control a control by requiring its impact closure to be empty.

items.method: the continuation is parsed back out of the frozen summary and read field by field; the delivered manifest.json and bundle.json are read off the worker's disk and compared byte-for-byte against what the service returned and what the store sealed. A dependent task is created so unfinished_commitments has real content to carry instead of an empty array, and a fact is applied to the profile so facts has content too - an empty-versus-empty comparison proves nothing.

items.obligation: CHG-PROPOSAL-NAMES-ITS-IMPACT belongs to this card, not to W06, because createChange fills impacted_refs and impact_link_ids deterministically
items.method: the skip is deleted. The applied requirement change's arrays are asserted by value: non-empty, every entry a shaped version reference, the closure required to reach beyond the edited entity and to contain both a Task and a DecisionReceipt, and every impact_link_id resolved back through GET /impact-links/{id} and required to be an ACTIVE DEPENDS_ON link. Where an empty closure is the correct answer - a proposal made while the project governs no decision - that is asserted as the expected empty value rather than skipped.

items.priority: assertion passes for the wrong reason
items.obligation: w0402.go:608 passed on 403 || 409 where the 403 was 'role not authorized' for a principal that holds no VERIFIER - the twin of the AA1 trap this card had already fixed
items.method: the disjunction is gone. The role leg pins status 403, protocol code FORBIDDEN and the 'role not authorized' reason; the independence leg pins 403, FORBIDDEN and 'author cannot independently accept'. A third assertion reads both principals' roles out of auth_principals rather than restating the fixture, and requires the two refusal reasons to differ, so neither can substitute for the other. The positive control that a VERIFIER-holding non-author is not refused here is CHG-INDEPENDENT-ACCEPTANCE-COMPUTED.

items.obligation: CTX-CONTEXT-READABLE-AGAIN-AFTER-RESTORE was never emitted in any run, because store.go's immutability trigger refuses the UPDATE; so the tamper refusal only ever exercised the storage branch and the service-side integrity check had zero coverage. That is the real reason Z3 survived.
items.product_change: none - the guard in materialize.go was already correct and untested
items.method: both layers now have their own control. The storage layer is asserted directly (the objects_immutable trigger refuses the write, and the bundle is still readable afterwards). Then the trigger is lifted on this throwaway fixture database so the service guard is the thing that refuses, the typed answer is pinned to 422 CONTENT_HASH_MISMATCH, and the trigger is put back and proven back by re-attempting the write it exists to refuse. A second service-side leg corrupts $.facts instead of $.summary and asserts the summary hash still matched, so the refusal can only have come from the receipt-hash half - without it, removing that half was unobservable, which is exactly how N4 survived the first time this matrix ran.
items.note_on_the_lifted_trigger: the database is a per-run temporary fixture under .local, not a delivered artifact; the trigger DDL is restored verbatim and CTX-STORAGE-IMMUTABILITY-TRIGGER-RESTORED asserts the restore by re-attempting the refused write. Nothing about the trigger is changed in migrations/.

items.disposition: SURVIVED, reported as an equivalent mutant with its proof rather than claimed as killed. createContext refuses with 412 STALE_REVISION unless Hash(state.revision) == Hash(b.expected_project_state_revision), so at the line N14 changes the two values are Hash-equal by construction and no assertion over the bundle can tell them apart.
